title: Tracking food accurately: weighing, labels, and common errors
chunks: Accurate tracking is what turns a calorie target into real results. Most people who feel 'stuck' are not in the deficit they think they are because of small, repeated tracking errors. A food scale and honest logging fix the majority of those errors.

Weigh foods in grams rather than using cups or 'eyeballing' portions, especially for calorie-dense items like oils, nut butters, cheese, nuts, granola, rice, and pasta. Volume measures and visual estimates can be off by 30–50% or more, which is enough to erase an entire deficit.

Weigh calorie-dense foods raw when possible and use the raw entry, since cooking changes weight as water is gained or lost. For example, 100 g of raw rice is very different from 100 g of cooked rice. Pick one convention (raw or cooked) per food and stay consistent.

Log everything, including the small extras: cooking oil, sauces, dressings, drinks with calories, bites while cooking, and 'just one' snacks. These untracked extras commonly add 200–500 hidden calories a day.

Food labels are allowed a margin of error and 'serving sizes' are often smaller than what people actually eat. Always check whether a value is per serving or per 100 g, and weigh your actual portion rather than trusting the package's serving estimate.

Use verified database entries when logging in Fitzenia, and prefer scanning a barcode or choosing entries that match the actual product. Generic entries vary widely in quality; a quick sanity check of the calories and protein per 100 g catches bad data.

You do not need to track forever. Weighing and logging carefully for a few weeks builds the awareness and portion intuition that let you maintain results more loosely later. Tracking is a skill you can dial up when you need precision and ease off once habits are set.
